problem:
Given that 
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}4xy-3{y}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}],$ 
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1).$

examples.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/af5524049f5f8b3c4c4241520f2d874b454d61b1b025362f5193437f766e610b.png)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/8882516e2732e419efdfb8439265212dd4f380d6a6ea58f6ff1291030bf50bfb.png)

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det \left( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \right)
$$

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/4fede2bb5c2306f62b55b7996488baee52c69e7d41b011e0e9d2b7405e63a8f4.png)

First, notice that since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/9252d1ce4f5df828f45351d01e0709cf2f2ca5df2c9c25390c111f40ca00fb22.png) we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = \ln y, 
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} = \dfrac xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{1}{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,1) = 0 \cdot 0 - 1\cdot 1 = -1.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2} & 2y({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y({x}^{2}-1))=4xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2})=4xy\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y({x}^{2}-1))=2({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & 4xy \\ 4xy & 2({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
